Volty / Vision

Built for work. Not just commuting.

Engineered for the daily rider covering 200 km on the job, our machines seamlessly transition from the workday grind to evening commutes, weekend rides, and coastal escapes. We deliver a single, durable motorcycle that matches your work ethic and delivers pure enjoyment when the shift is over.

What We Are Building

The pickup truck of electric bikes.

Designed for work rather than mere commuting, Volty is a utility-first electric motorcycle platform. Its flat, modular frame directly addresses the practical demands of delivery services, ride-hailing, and last-mile logistics across Vietnamese cities.

While most electric two-wheelers target lifestyle buyers, Volty prioritizes the demands of daily labor. Built for riders who log 200 km daily, performance is measured in uptime, payload capacity, and operating costs. Yet this same machine is their go-to ride on Sundays.

These are not separate audiences; they are the exact same individual. A motorcycle crafted with the integrity required to earn a living is inherently a motorcycle worth riding for enjoyment.

The Thesis

Design with a purpose.

The U1 was built for the working rider. Every single feature is a direct response to real-world demands, starting with the job itself rather than an aesthetic silhouette. Function dictates form:

  • A rack is included because cargo needs to be transported.
  • A swappable battery pack prevents costly downtime.
  • An easily serviceable drivetrain keeps the bike out of the shop and actively earning.

We eliminate decorative styling and hold every component accountable; if a part does not earn its place, it gets cut. When purpose drives design, form becomes a statement rather than mere ornament.

Resisting unnecessary features is difficult, but we refuse to build showroom vehicles loaded with unrequested extras. To stay true to our mission, the U1 must meet two strict criteria:

  1. Does it assist the rider in earning a living? If no, it is omitted.
  2. Is it a bike someone would still want to ride after their shift? If no, we have merely crafted an appliance.
How We Build

Four rules, no exceptions.

Far from a simple mood board, our design philosophy consists of four core commitments against which every decision is evaluated.

01

Design with purpose

Function is the brief. If a part cannot justify its cost in the rider's day, it is not on the bike.

02

Focus on a need

We build for one rider: the person who earns a living on two wheels. The same person who rides for the joy of it after the last drop-off. We design for the work first, because a bike that survives the work is more than good enough for the weekend.

03

Solve a specific problem

Fuel that tracks the pump price. Downtime that eats wages. A bike that cannot carry the load. We fix those, precisely, rather than everything vaguely.

04

Be meaningful

A vehicle earns meaning when it changes a rider's economics, and keeps it when they choose to ride it on a day nobody is paying them to.

The Responsibility

What we owe the road.

Designing vehicles for working riders is a critical responsibility because they rely on these machines for their livelihood. Network failures cause lost shifts, cost errors impose financial burdens, and safety compromises put lives at risk. Therefore, we hold ourselves to the highest standards for a tool that families depend on.

We also serve urban communities such as Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi as they transition away from gasoline. Riders should not have to sacrifice income to adopt electric vehicles. Environmental benefits must be accompanied by lower operational costs so that sustainable mobility is accessible and profitable for everyone.

The Future

Mobility that means something.

The evolution of mobility relies on designing vehicles with a clear purpose, rather than expanding production scale. Sustainable market leadership will belong to organizations dedicated to solving real human challenges, rather than those appealing broadly with superficial objectives.

Our core focus is well-defined: to engineer practical electric vehicles for working people in key urban areas, built to a high enough standard to serve as their primary choice off the job as well. We are committed to proving that focused engineering and viable enterprise reinforce each other rather than conflict.

The Vietnam we are building toward: the rider who moves the city can afford the machine that moves them, and still wants to ride it on the one day nobody is paying for the trip. Meaningful is not a claim we make. It is the specification we are held to.

"Design with a purpose. Focus on a need. Solve a specific problem. Everything else is noise."
